Lee (Solutions): New POC with ClearPath Health. They need private connectivity, static outbound IPs for allowlists, and answers for security questionnaire.
Tara (NetEng): Ok. Do they insist on preserving original client IPs? That determines peering vs PrivateLink.
Lee (Solutions): Their compliance team prefers no peering if possible, but audit logs must show client identity.
Omar (AE): Pricing check: 30-day POC, 1 AZ PrivateDeploy, 2 static EIPs. Any setup fees?
Tara (NetEng): PrivateLink avoids peering approvals. Note: PrivateLink NATs traffic at our ENI so original private src IP won't be visible. Recommend X-Forwarded-For header and mutual TLS to prove header integrity.
Nina (Security): For the questionnaire: confirm customer-managed KMS support (yes via cross-account roles), VPC Flow Logs export (yes), and SOC2 link. Also list HSM partners for FIPS needs.
Tara (NetEng): SNI allowlist example for their perimeter appliance and MTU guidance for S2S tunnels:
```
# SNI allowlist example
match tls.sni == "api.clearpath.svc.redwood.ai" -> allow
# Tunnel MTU
set mtu 1400
set mss 1360
```
Lee (Solutions): If they refuse an egress proxy, propose Dedicated PrivateDeploy with managed NAT EIPs (we provide static egress). We'll document tradeoffs.
Omar (AE): I'll gather budget and confirm whether they can run an egress proxy.
Tara (NetEng): Quick firewall snippet (customer egress):
```
allow tcp any 443 to 34.122.210.10  # PrivateLink ENI AZ1 example
allow udp any 53 to 10.0.0.2       # DNS
```
Nina (Security): Add note: recommend mTLS between customer egress proxy and our endpoint if header authenticity is required.
Lee (Solutions): Action items: Tara -> add network answers to questionnaire; Nina -> attach SOC2 & HSM notes; Omar -> confirm proxy & budget. Demo scheduled Thu 9am PT.
Omar (AE): ack
Tara (NetEng): ack
Nina (Security): ack
